subject: Urgent: routing policy exception request + customer-ready update
messages:
From: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@blueshift.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Sudden latency spike and throughput drop — production impact

Marissa,

We are seeing a sustained latency spike across our inference routes in us-east-1 starting ~08:50 ET (roughly 22:50 UTC).  P95 has jumped from ~140 ms to 1.1s and overall throughput dropped by ~40%.  This is affecting our ingestion pipeline and a few downstream UI calls.

We captured a short perf trace and a KV snapshot and have attached them here (perf-trace-20260701.jsonl). Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side or if there's something we should change in our routing?

We need an ETA on mitigation — any chance you can escalate?

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Lead
BlueShift Analytics

[Attachment: perf-trace-20260701.jsonl]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: SRE Team <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@blueshift.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:18:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden latency spike and throughput drop — production impact

Team — forwarding BlueShift's report. Summary: P95 ~1.1s, throughput -40% from ~08:50 ET. They've attached a perf trace and KV snapshot. They are asking for confirmation if this is on our side and an ETA to mitigate.

Asks:
- Can SRE triage immediately and confirm root cause or narrow to routing/runtime?
- If this is capacity-related (batching / node saturation / kernel fallback), we may need a temporary routing policy exception to route BlueShift to a compatible higher-capacity pool or allow warm fallback to the next model variant for up to 2 hours. Product (Maya) — need a quick decision on exceptions and customer communication tone.

Priority: high — customer is seeing production impact. I left them on Cc so they see we're working it.

Attachments: perf-trace-20260701.jsonl, kvsnapshot-1100.bin

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: kvsnapshot-1100.bin]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:27:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency spike and throughput drop — production impact

On Tue, 01 Jul 2026 at 09:18, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding BlueShift's report.

I've started an SRE sandbox triage and pulled the provided perf-trace. Initial findings: around the time they reported — we see an increase in kernel-level stalls on several serving nodes in us-east-1, coincident with elevated long-tail for > 2k token requests. There is also an uptick in eviction events on the KV cache for that customer because of a sequence of larger-than-usual prefix loads.

Immediate mitigation attempt I'm running now: 1) bumping their routing weight to prefer lower-concurrency nodes within their Dedicated pool; 2) temporarily disabling aggressive batching for their critical routes to prevent large queue head-of-line blocking.  Expect ~10-12 minutes to see changes in telemetry.

If that doesn't stabilize P95, next step is to carve a short-lived routing exception to route them to a higher-capacity pool (requires product/ops sign-off). I'll post telemetry in ~10.

- Sean
Senior SRE
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

[Included: excerpt from perf-trace — summary lines]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency spike and throughput drop — production impact

On Tue, 01 Jul 2026 at 09:27, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've started an SRE sandbox triage and pulled the provided perf-trace.

More detail from runtime side: we are seeing kernel fallback patterns on a subset of model shards — likely caused by mixed sequence lengths and a temporary cache misalignment that caused increased memory pressure. The KV evictions Sean noted line up with an aggressive prefix-heavy test that BlueShift ran at 08:45 (their trace shows repeated long prompts).

Mitigation plan I can implement if SRE adjustments don't fully recover:
- Apply a routing policy exception for BlueShift to route to the higher-memory pool (pool-bigh-1) for up to 90 minutes. This requires product approval and an ops change (I can do the change and pre-stage rollback).
- Persisting: we should add a targeted KV time-to-live increase for their critical prefixes to reduce thrashing (longer-term fix).

If Sean's initial config change shows improvement in <15m, hold on the exception. If not, I'll enact the pooling change once we get product sign-off.

-Hannah
Principal SWE (Serving Runtime)
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:50:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency spike and throughput drop — production impact

Thanks for the quick triage. Decision guidance: approve a temporary routing policy exception to pool-bigh-1 for a maximum of 90 minutes, but only if SRE/Hannah confirm that Sean's config tweaks do not restore P95 within the next 15 minutes. Constraints:
- Exception must be logged in the incident record (SUP-4721) with reason and rollback window.
- Notify customer with a short, non-technical update (Marissa to send) and commit to a follow-up engineering postmortem within 48 hours.
- No billing credits unless the postmortem finds a causal bug on our side.

Please proceed on that basis. Hannah/Sean — flag me if you need me to be on the call.

-Maya
VP Product (Serving)
maya_srinivasan@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@blueshift.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Sudden latency spike and throughput drop — production impact

Tom — quick update from Redwood: our SREs have made a targeted configuration change to reduce aggressive batching for your critical routes and are monitoring telemetry now. If latency does not recover within 15 minutes, we have product approval to apply a short-lived routing exception to move your traffic to a larger-capacity pool for up to 90 minutes while we stabilize things.

We will:
- Monitor P95 and throughput for the next 15 minutes and confirm by 10:20 ET;
- If needed, apply the exception and notify you with timing;
- Run a follow-up postmortem within 48 hours and share findings.

Appreciate the perf trace — that helped narrow down the root patterns. Will keep you posted.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
